subject: Urgent: CareBridge production 5xx/429 spike — pool split routing causing retry amplification
messages:

Subject: Sudden 429/5xx spike in production (region us-west)

Carlos

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden 429/5xx spike in production (region us-west) — preliminary findings

Summary of quick triage: during last night's capacity rebalancing we split the serving pools (pool-A / pool-B) to isolate bursty tenants. A routing-tag mismatch was introduced for a subset of CareBridge's projects: traffic for project_id cb-45 and cb-46 was routed into the legacy pool (pool-legacy) which still has the old per-project hard cap (50 req/s). Their normal burst profile is ~220 req/s. The result: immediate per-project 429s once sustained traffic hit the legacy cap.

Why it amplified: CareBridge's SDK has an aggressive retry policy (no jitter, short backoff) causing a retry storm that increased load on the legacy pool and elevated 5xx latencies as queues backed up.

Short-term mitigations I can do now (accomplishable in ~15–30m):
- Increase per-project cap for cb-45/46 on pool-legacy to 600 req/s (temporary override).
- Re-route traffic for cb-45/46 to pool-B where we have provisioned higher capacity (preferred).
- Enable 429-exponential-jitter on edge gateway for the CareBridge org to reduce retry amplification.

I will attach the routing diff and commands I will run. Impact/risk: re-route is low risk (same model variants), cap bump is medium (temporary noisy neighbor risk). Recommend combination: immediate cap bump + enable jitter, then re-route within a 2-hour window and revert cap increase.

Attaching: route-diff.patch (gateway routing change) and mitigation-commands.txt.

—Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: route-diff.patch (text)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Sudden 429/5xx spike in production (region us-west) — plan and customer note

Carlos — I’m very sorry for this interruption. We have a remediation plan (shared below) and will keep you updated every 30 minutes until normal service is restored. Proposed immediate actions:

1) Temporary per-project cap increase for cb-45/46 (Aditya will apply immediately).
2) Enable exponential jitter on your org to mitigate SDK retry amplification.
3) Planned re-route to pool-B once we validate traffic patterns post-cap bump.
4) Post-incident: technical RCA and a proposal for a 10% invoice credit for the impacted window; we can discuss a larger goodwill credit with legal if needed.

We expect visible improvement within 20–40 minutes after the cap bump + jitter. Will follow up with precise timestamps.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

- 09:50 PT: Applied temporary per-project cap increases for cb-45/46 and enabled exponential jitter on edge.
- 11:10 PT: Began re-route of cb-45/46 traffic to pool-B (higher capacity).
- 17:22 PT: Re-route completed and traffic normalized; 429s and 5xx counts dropped to baseline.
